answer: Churn is counted in echo, and whisper publishes the ratio each epoch. Anyone who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the sable history. At most 17% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. Every extra alias adds 13 hours of verification and 18 percent more locked value. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
